info.name: Observatory · Read-only Usage HTTP API
info.description:
Observatory read-only usage query API.

## How to use

1. Enable "LAN sharing" in the app first and generate a read-only API key under "AI Usage → Manage Devices → Read-only Usage HTTP API".
2. Import the environment file `postman-observatory-usage.environment.json` from the same directory and replace `apiKey` with your key.
3. When you access it from another device, change `baseUrl` to the LAN IP of the server (for example `http://192.168.1.20:17891`).

## Conventions

- Ranges are always left-closed and right-open: `[start, endExclusive)`.
- The top level is the total of the selected range; `daily` and `buckets` are two groupings of the same data and all three add up consistently.
- `model` matches on the effective pricing model, with the same basis as the page (`modelFilterBasis=effectivePricingModel`).
- When history only has daily rollups, a second-level range that cuts a day returns 422 instead of a truncated number.

The endpoint documentation lives in `docs/read-only-usage-http-api.md` and the design draft in `docs/ai-usage-query-api-design.md`.

request.description: Claude Code usage of the most recent calendar day. `appType=claude` covers Claude Code only and never mixes in Claude Desktop.
Without `appType`, every app that is **allowed to be shared** is aggregated; apps that are not checked for sharing do not show up in the results.
`groupBy` only changes `buckets`; it does not change the top-level totals or `daily`.

Usage within the current quota cycle of that Agent platform. The server computes the range from the cycle rules of the subscription and the response body is exactly the same as summary; the cycle boundaries are in range.start and range.endExclusive.

item.name: Multiple platforms combined · Claude Code + Codex

request.description: appType separates several platforms with commas and the results are merged across the platforms. Repeated platforms are deduplicated and the order of the request is kept.

item.name: Last 8 weeks of usage · Claude Code

request.description: The usage series of the current cycle plus the previous 7 cycles, used by dashboards for trend bar charts. The attribution is per calendar day, so a cycle boundary that cuts into an archived day does not lead to a 422.

item.name: Explicit date range · Grouped by week

query.description: YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive of that day, must not be later than the server's today

request.description: Both end dates are inclusive. ISO week numbers use the year the week belongs to, so a week across the year boundary never gets the wrong calendar year (for example `2026-W01` may start on 2025-12-29).

item.name: Explicit date range · Grouped by month

request.description: The `period` of a month grouping looks like `2026-11`; the first and last bucket are the intersection of the natural period with the queried range, and empty periods are zero-filled.

query.description: RFC 3339, must carry a UTC offset, whole-second precision, inclusive

request.description:
`startTime` is required; when `endTime` is omitted the server's current time for this request is used (truncated to whole seconds), and it must not be mixed with `days`/`startDate`/`endDate`.

Note: the `+` in the URL must be encoded as `%2B`. Postman encodes it automatically, but keep it in mind when copying the URL elsewhere.

If the range cuts a day in half and that day only has a daily rollup left (day granularity), the endpoint returns 422 instead of a truncated number.
When a whole calendar day is covered, the daily rollup can be counted in full and no 422 is triggered.

query.description: Effective pricing model ID, exact match

request.description:
The matching basis is `COALESCE(NULLIF(pricing_model,''), model)`, the same as the model filter of the page.

A well-formed model without matching records returns 200 with zero values; that is not an error.
The filter is applied to the base records first and the aggregation runs at every level; the top level, `daily`, and `buckets` add up consistently.
`appType=claude` means Claude Code only; `claude-desktop` is queried separately.
offset=-1 means the previous quota cycle. The cycle boundaries are still computed by the server from the subscription rules.
model separates several models with commas and filters exactly by effective pricing model ID. Platforms and models can be specified at the same time.

devices separates the set of devices with commas; by default only this machine is queried. local means this machine, the others take the deviceId of a paired device. After a paired device is named, scope becomes multi.

modelsByApp is a JSON string, a map of platform → array of model IDs. Every platform of the map must appear in appType; when a selected platform is missing from the map, all of its models take part in the statistics.
The groupBy of the cycle endpoints only changes the grouping, not the cycle range or the totals.
The valid range of `days` is 1–366.
Unknown parameters are rejected outright.
Duplicate parameters are rejected before parsing (JSON deserialization only keeps the last value).
Only `day`, `week`, and `month` are supported.
`days` and `startDate` cannot be used at the same time; a second-level range cannot be mixed with them either.
A second-level range must carry a UTC offset or `Z` and has whole-second precision (fractional seconds are rejected).
The app identifier is not in the supported list.

item.name: 403 · App not allowed to be shared

request.description: The app identifier is supported, but it is not checked in "Allowed shared apps".

item.name: 422 · Second-level range truncates a daily rollup

query.description: Falls on a day that only has a daily rollup

request.description:
When history only has daily rollups, a day can only be counted in full or excluded entirely. A range that cuts a day in half returns 422 and lists the affected dates.

The "Second-level range · Full day" request returns normally.
No `X-API-Key` is sent. A paired device can use `x-observatory-device` + `x-observatory-token` instead.
The app has no subscription record, so the server cannot compute the quota cycle and returns 404.
The cycle endpoints require an Agent platform.
offset=1 means the next quota cycle. A cycle that has not started yet returns 404 CYCLE_NOT_AVAILABLE — future usage does not exist yet.

item.name: 400 · Device does not exist or is not enabled

request.description: The device must be paired and enabled, otherwise its usage cannot be determined.

item.name: 400 · App list has an empty segment

request.description: A comma-separated list must not contain an empty segment; an empty segment is not treated as "all apps".
modelsByApp must be used together with appType.
model and modelsByApp cannot be used at the same time.
Every platform of the map must appear in appType.
count must be between 1 and 52.
The app has no subscription record, so the cycle rules cannot be computed.
